intro.title: Message Queues & Event-Driven
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple event-driven notification system using a message queue. You will learn how to decouple services by having a producer send messages and a consumer process them asynchronously. The core concept is the publish-subscribe pattern, which enables scalable and resilient communication between components. You will implement this using a simulated message queue to understand how events are queued and handled without direct coupling.
intro.usecase: Message queues and event-driven architecture are the backbone of scalable, real-time applications you use daily. For example, when you add an item to your cart on an e-commerce site, a message queue decouples the UI click from backend processes like inventory checks and order confirmation emails, ensuring the interface stays responsive. In a live dashboard tracking social media analytics, an event-driven system processes incoming posts and updates charts without blocking user interactions. As a developer, you'll implement this pattern to build resilient features like real-time notifications, activity feeds, or any system where services need to communicate asynchronously without tight coupling.
